speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo. To help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly what these episodes feel like and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the positional nature of your spinning episodes is very helpful. Given your age and hearing history, have you noticed any new ringing in your ears (tinnitus) or a feeling of fullness in your ear when these episodes occur?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming; the positional nature of your vertigo is a key finding. Have you noticed any imbalance while walking, or any numbness or weakness on one side of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for providing your history; the absence of neurological deficits and prior ear conditions narrows the possibilities. To confirm the specific type of positional vertigo, I need to know if the spinning sensation lasts less than one minute and if you have a history of similar attacks in the past.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
